source.name: Escape in a nested menubar submenu must close only that submenu and return focus to its parent item
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/NickDJM/accessible-menu/issues/533) at 4b8e65db81f40c0c032db1c8567615bbe3da32f6. Blind to the maintainers' fix cfb4dc85f57e59c3e1ca3c8835618101a6e818b9; routing auto.

journey.title: Escape closes only the innermost open submenu
journey.goal: Escape in the Facts submenu returns to Facts while the About submenu stays open

functionalJourney.title: Open nested submenus with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: About and Facts submenus open on click

guards.title: Escape in a first-level submenu returns to the menubar
guards.goal: Escape in the About submenu closes it and focuses About

plan.root_cause: The Escape key handler for submenus incorrectly calls this.elements.rootMenu.closeChildren(), which closes all submenus of the root menu, instead of closing only the current submenu.
plan.repair_strategy: In menubar.js, replace the Escape handling in the non-top-level case of _handleKeyup to close the current submenu via its toggle on the parent menu item and move focus to that parent menu item.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will close only the innermost open submenu and return focus to its parent menu item, preserving the state of other open submenus.
functional_risks: If a submenu somehow lacks a parent menu item or toggle, the close could fail, but this condition cannot occur in the current menu structure.
Ensure that the change does not affect Escape behavior when no submenu is open (should remain unchanged).
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape in the Facts submenu returns focus to the Facts item and keeps the About submenu open (aria-expanded true).
Verify that pressing Escape in the About submenu returns focus to the About item and closes the About submenu.
Verify that pressing Escape when no submenu is open does not alter the menubar state.
Verify that Arrow navigation (Right, Down, Left, Up) continues to work as expected after the change.
